title: Component Biomass
text: four functions share argument structure treeCalc(). Summing four components reproduces treeCalc() result exactly: Component proportions vary species tree size:
code: wood <- woodCalc(   data    = sample_trees, eval = "ung_2",   species = "SPECIES", dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT",   output  = "biomass", decay = FALSE ) #> Output: biomass (kg)  bark <- suppressMessages(barkCalc(   data    = sample_trees, eval = "ung_2",   species = "SPECIES", dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT",   output  = "biomass", decay = FALSE ))  branch <- suppressMessages(branchCalc(   data       = sample_trees, eval = "ung_2",   species    = "SPECIES",    dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT",   crown_cond = "CROWN_COND", output = "biomass", decay = FALSE ))  foliage <- suppressMessages(foliageCalc(   data       = sample_trees, eval = "ung_2",   species    = "SPECIES",    dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT",   crown_cond = "CROWN_COND", output = "biomass", decay = FALSE )) agb <- suppressMessages(   treeCalc(sample_trees, eval = "ung_2", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT", crown_cond = "CROWN_COND",            output = "biomass", decay = FALSE) ) all.equal(wood + bark + branch + foliage, agb) #> [1] TRUE total <- wood + bark + branch + foliage data.frame(   species = sample_trees$SPECIES,   wood_pct    = round(wood    / total * 100, 1),   bark_pct    = round(bark    / total * 100, 1),   branch_pct  = round(branch  / total * 100, 1),   foliage_pct = round(foliage / total * 100, 1) ) #>    species wood_pct bark_pct branch_pct foliage_pct #> 1 PSEU_MEN     60.2     10.3       18.9        10.6 #> 2 PINU_CON     74.4      7.7       11.2         6.6 #> 3 TSUG_HET     67.2     10.2       14.0         8.7 #> 4 POPU_TRE     71.2     15.3       11.6         1.9 #> 5 PICE_MAR     70.0     12.4        7.8         9.8 #> 6 PICE_GLA     76.6      8.6        9.7         5.1

title: Component Biomass
text: barkCalc() accepts optional rem_bark column (percentage remaining, 0-100). scales bark biomass proportionally useful trees beetle kill, fire scorch, logging damage.
code: sample_trees$REM_BARK <- c(100, 100, 80, 60, 20, 100)  full_bark <- suppressMessages(   barkCalc(sample_trees, eval = "ung_2", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT", output = "biomass", decay = FALSE) ) partial_bark <- suppressMessages(   barkCalc(sample_trees, eval = "ung_2", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT", rem_bark = "REM_BARK",            output = "biomass", decay = FALSE) )  data.frame(   species  = sample_trees$SPECIES,   rem_bark = sample_trees$REM_BARK,   full_kg  = round(full_bark,    2),   adj_kg   = round(partial_bark, 2) ) #>    species rem_bark full_kg adj_kg #> 1 PSEU_MEN      100   46.44  46.44 #> 2 PINU_CON      100    8.16   8.16 #> 3 TSUG_HET       80    4.50   3.60 #> 4 POPU_TRE       60   46.05  27.63 #> 5 PICE_MAR       20    2.54   0.51 #> 6 PICE_GLA      100   61.83  61.83

title: Component Biomass
text: jenkinsRatio() decomposes total -ground biomass four component proportions using Jenkins et al. (2003) equations. requires DBH species — height crown condition. Species classified softwood hardwood internally. element vector ratios (one per tree). Jenkins equations fit independently per component, four components sum approximately 1 rather exactly 1: Multiply ratios Jenkins total biomass estimate get component values. Note coarse_root Jenkins-derived estimate uses different equations rootCalc(), applies Li et al. (2003):
code: ratios <- jenkinsRatio(sample_trees, dbh = "DBH", species = "SPECIES") #> Output: component ratios (foliage, coarse_roots, stem_bark, stem_wood) str(ratios) #> List of 4 #>  $ foliage     : num [1:6] 0.0596 0.0659 0.0711 0.0209 0.082 ... #>  $ coarse_roots: num [1:6] 0.214 0.217 0.22 0.19 0.224 ... #>  $ stem_bark   : num [1:6] 0.118 0.115 0.113 0.126 0.109 ... #>  $ stem_wood   : num [1:6] 0.651 0.625 0.606 0.605 0.572 ... wood_type <- SPECIES_CLASS$WOOD_TYPE[   match(sample_trees$SPECIES, SPECIES_CLASS$SPECIES) ]  data.frame(   species     = sample_trees$SPECIES,   wood_type   = wood_type,   foliage     = round(ratios$foliage,      3),   coarse_root = round(ratios$coarse_roots, 3),   stem_bark   = round(ratios$stem_bark,    3),   stem_wood   = round(ratios$stem_wood,    3),   check_sum   = round(ratios$foliage + ratios$coarse_roots +                         ratios$stem_bark + ratios$stem_wood, 3) ) #>    species wood_type foliage coarse_root stem_bark stem_wood check_sum #> 1 PSEU_MEN  softwood   0.060       0.214     0.118     0.651     1.043 #> 2 PINU_CON  softwood   0.066       0.217     0.115     0.625     1.023 #> 3 TSUG_HET  softwood   0.071       0.220     0.113     0.606     1.010 #> 4 POPU_TRE  hardwood   0.021       0.190     0.126     0.605     0.941 #> 5 PICE_MAR  softwood   0.082       0.224     0.109     0.572     0.988 #> 6 PICE_GLA  softwood   0.058       0.213     0.119     0.659     1.049 jenkins_total <- suppressMessages(   treeCalc(sample_trees, eval = "jenkins", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", output = "biomass", decay = FALSE) )  data.frame(   species     = sample_trees$SPECIES,   stem_wood   = round(ratios$stem_wood    * jenkins_total, 1),   stem_bark   = round(ratios$stem_bark    * jenkins_total, 1),   foliage     = round(ratios$foliage      * jenkins_total, 1),   coarse_root = round(ratios$coarse_roots * jenkins_total, 1) ) #>    species stem_wood stem_bark foliage coarse_root #> 1 PSEU_MEN     343.5      62.5    31.4       113.0 #> 2 PINU_CON      60.1      11.1     6.3        20.9 #> 3 TSUG_HET      34.6       6.5     4.1        12.6 #> 4 POPU_TRE     182.4      37.9     6.3        57.3 #> 5 PICE_MAR      14.7       2.8     2.1         5.8 #> 6 PICE_GLA     484.7      87.8    42.6       156.8

title: Getting Started with ForestBiomass
text: treeCalc() requires data frame one row per tree. package includes sample_trees, six-tree dataset covering common BC species: required columns :
code: sample_trees #>    SPECIES  DBH HEIGHT APPEARANCE CROWN_COND #> 1 PSEU_MEN 32.4   22.1          1          1 #> 2 PINU_CON 18.7   14.5          1          2 #> 3 TSUG_HET 14.2   11.8          3          3 #> 4 POPU_TRE 27.6   20.3          2          1 #> 5 PICE_MAR  9.8    8.4          5          4 #> 6 PICE_GLA 41.3   28.7          1          1

title: Getting Started with ForestBiomass
text: treeCalc() eval = "ung_2" (default) uses Ung et al. (2008) equations BC species, fitting biomass function DBH height. value total -ground biomass one tree kilograms. decay = TRUE applies species-specific reduction standing dead downed wood (Harmon et al., 2011). live-tree inventories, use decay = FALSE.
code: agb <- treeCalc(   data       = sample_trees,   eval       = "ung_2",   species    = "SPECIES",   dbh        = "DBH",   height     = "HEIGHT",   appearance = "APPEARANCE",   crown_cond = "CROWN_COND",   output     = "biomass",   decay      = TRUE ) #> Output: biomass (kg) #> Species specified decay reduction factor applied (Harmon et al., 2011) agb #> [1] 452.36300 106.23299  39.83234 300.01647  20.34684 721.02620

title: Getting Started with ForestBiomass
text: output argument controls units whether result carbon: plot_radius argument controls per-hectare expansion factor:
code: # Per-tree biomass (kg) — default suppressMessages(   treeCalc(sample_trees, eval = "ung_2", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT", appearance = "APPEARANCE",            crown_cond = "CROWN_COND", output = "biomass", decay = FALSE) ) #> [1] 452.36300 106.23299  44.25815 300.01647  20.53162 721.02620  # Per-tree carbon (kg) — biomass × 0.5 suppressMessages(   treeCalc(sample_trees, eval = "ung_2", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT", appearance = "APPEARANCE",            crown_cond = "CROWN_COND", output = "carbon", decay = FALSE) ) #> [1] 226.18150  53.11649  22.12908 150.00823  10.26581 360.51310  # Stand-level biomass (Mg/ha) — requires plot_radius suppressMessages(   treeCalc(sample_trees, eval = "ung_2", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT", appearance = "APPEARANCE",            crown_cond = "CROWN_COND", output = "biomass Mg/ha",            decay = FALSE, plot_radius = 11.28) ) #> [1] 11.3090750  2.6558247  1.1064539  7.5004117  0.5132905 18.0256551  # Stand-level carbon (Mg/ha) suppressMessages(   treeCalc(sample_trees, eval = "ung_2", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT", appearance = "APPEARANCE",            crown_cond = "CROWN_COND", output = "carbon Mg/ha",            decay = FALSE, plot_radius = 11.28) ) #> [1] 5.6545375 1.3279123 0.5532269 3.7502058 0.2566453 9.0128275

title: Getting Started with ForestBiomass
text: Five eval options available: "ung_1" "ung_2" use 17 BC species. Use "lambert_1" "lambert_2" Eastern Canada species (see ?LAMBERT_1). "jenkins" pathway covers species JENKINS_GROUPS requires height crown condition measurement.

title: Getting Started with ForestBiomass
text: decay = TRUE (default), species-specific decay class reduction factor applied Harmon et al. (2011). Trees appearance code 1 (freshly dead / recently fallen) receive reduction; higher codes apply increasing reductions. Live trees use decay = FALSE.
code: no_decay   <- suppressMessages(   treeCalc(sample_trees, eval = "ung_2", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT", appearance = "APPEARANCE",            crown_cond = "CROWN_COND", output = "biomass", decay = FALSE) ) with_decay <- suppressMessages(   treeCalc(sample_trees, eval = "ung_2", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT", appearance = "APPEARANCE",            crown_cond = "CROWN_COND", output = "biomass", decay = TRUE) )  data.frame(   species    = sample_trees$SPECIES,   appearance = sample_trees$APPEARANCE,   no_decay   = round(no_decay,   1),   with_decay = round(with_decay, 1),   pct_reduction = round((1 - with_decay / no_decay) * 100, 1) ) #>    species appearance no_decay with_decay pct_reduction #> 1 PSEU_MEN          1    452.4      452.4           0.0 #> 2 PINU_CON          1    106.2      106.2           0.0 #> 3 TSUG_HET          3     44.3       39.8          10.0 #> 4 POPU_TRE          2    300.0      300.0           0.0 #> 5 PICE_MAR          5     20.5       20.3           0.9 #> 6 PICE_GLA          1    721.0      721.0           0.0

title: Getting Started with ForestBiomass
text: height crown condition unavailable, eval = "jenkins" estimates total -ground biomass directly DBH alone:
code: treeCalc(   data       = sample_trees,   eval       = "jenkins",   species    = "SPECIES",   dbh        = "DBH",   appearance = "APPEARANCE",   output     = "biomass",   decay      = TRUE ) #> Output: biomass (kg) #> Species specified decay reduction factor applied (Harmon et al., 2011) #> [1] 527.67476  96.13723  51.41830 301.63899  25.45366 735.73324

title: Getting Started with ForestBiomass
text: rootCalc() applies Li et al. (2003) root equations pre-computed -ground biomass column. requires -ground biomass Mg/ha (kg plot_radius conversion). Fine coarse root fractions can returned separately:
code: sample_trees$AGB <- suppressMessages(   treeCalc(sample_trees, eval = "ung_2", species = "SPECIES",            dbh = "DBH", height = "HEIGHT", appearance = "APPEARANCE",            crown_cond = "CROWN_COND", output = "biomass Mg/ha",            decay = TRUE, plot_radius = 11.28) )  rootCalc(   data      = sample_trees,   biomass   = "AGB",   species   = "SPECIES",   units     = "Mg/ha",   root_type = "total",   output    = "biomass Mg/ha" ) #> Input units: Mg/ha #> Output: biomass Mg/ha #> Root type: total #> [1] 2.5106147 0.5895931 0.2210695 5.4416869 0.1129249 4.0016954 fine   <- suppressMessages(   rootCalc(sample_trees, biomass = "AGB", species = "SPECIES",            units = "Mg/ha", root_type = "fine") ) coarse <- suppressMessages(   rootCalc(sample_trees, biomass = "AGB", species = "SPECIES",            units = "Mg/ha", root_type = "coarse") ) total  <- suppressMessages(   rootCalc(sample_trees, biomass = "AGB", species = "SPECIES",            units = "Mg/ha", root_type = "total") )  data.frame(   species = sample_trees$SPECIES,   fine    = round(fine,   3),   coarse  = round(coarse, 3),   total   = round(total,  3) ) #>    species  fine coarse total #> 1 PSEU_MEN 0.945  1.565 2.511 #> 2 PINU_CON 0.244  0.346 0.590 #> 3 TSUG_HET 0.093  0.128 0.221 #> 4 POPU_TRE 1.782  3.660 5.442 #> 5 PICE_MAR 0.048  0.065 0.113 #> 6 PICE_GLA 1.402  2.599 4.002

title: ForestBiomass
text: ForestBiomass R package estimating tree biomass carbon Canadian temperate forests. implements hierarchical allometric equations component level (wood, bark, branches, foliage) supports total -ground -ground biomass estimation. Decay class reduction factors can applied standing dead wood.

title: Bark Calculation — barkCalc
text: data User specified dataframe. eval allomentic equation used? Default "ung_2". Options : "ung_1", "ung_2", "lambert_1", "lambert_2". dbh Column within data Diameter Breast Height (dbh) specified. height Optional. Required lambert_2 ung_2. species Column within data species specified. NFI codes species. appearance Optional. Required decay = TRUE. rem_bark Optional. Column within data remaining bark percentage (0-100) specified. output One "biomass" (kg, default), "biomass Mg/ha", "carbon" (kg), "carbon Mg/ha". decay Logical default = TRUE. decay class reduction factor applied? plot_radius Plot radius metres. Required output "biomass Mg/ha" "carbon Mg/ha". Must one 3.99, 5.64, 7.98, 11.28. Default 11.28 m.

title: Tree Biomass Calculation — treeCalc
text: Calculates total -ground tree biomass carbon. Two methodologies available: (1) summing wood, branch, foliage, bark components using allometric equations Ung et al., 2008 Lambert et al., 2005; (2) direct total -ground biomass via Jenkins et al., 2003 national-scale equations. species-specific decay class reduction factor (Harmon et al., 2011) can applied.

title: Tree Biomass Calculation — treeCalc
code: treeCalc(   data,   eval = "ung_2",   dbh,   height = NULL,   species,   appearance = NULL,   crown_cond = NULL,   rem_bark = NULL,   output = "biomass",   decay = TRUE,   plot_radius = 11.28 )

title: Tree Biomass Calculation — treeCalc
text: data User specified dataframe. eval equation set use. Default "ung_2". Options : "ung_1", "ung_2", "lambert_1", "lambert_2" (component-sum pathway), "jenkins" (Jenkins et al., 2003 direct total biomass). dbh Column within data Diameter Breast Height (dbh) specified. height Optional. Required "lambert_2" "ung_2". species Column within data species specified. NFI codes species. appearance Optional. Required decay = TRUE. crown_cond Column within data crown condition specified. Required "ung_1", "ung_2", "lambert_1", "lambert_2". used "jenkins". rem_bark Optional. Column within data remaining bark percentage (0-100) specified. used "jenkins". output One "biomass" (kg, default), "biomass Mg/ha", "carbon" (kg), "carbon Mg/ha". decay Logical default = TRUE. decay class reduction factor applied? plot_radius Plot radius metres. Required output "biomass Mg/ha" "carbon Mg/ha". Must one 3.99, 5.64, 7.98, 11.28. Default 11.28 m.
